# CoProducer — full assistant digest

Updated: 2026-10-18

## Parallel compression sounds thin? Check the latency first
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/parallel-compression-sounds-thin-check-latency.html
Parallel compression making drums or vocals thinner? The parallel bus is probably arriving late. Find the offset, fix the timing, then dial it in.
Keywords: parallel compression, parallel compression sounds thin, New York compression, plugin delay compensation, comb filtering, null test, phase drum bus, latency, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Why your gapless album gets gaps after MP3 or AAC
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/gapless-album-gaps-after-mp3-or-aac.html
MP3 and AAC encoders add silence at the start and padding at the end of every file. Why segues break, what we measured, and how to stay seamless.
Keywords: gapless playback, gap between tracks, encoder delay, MP3 gapless, AAC priming, LAME tag, album segue, continuous mix, DDP, NoDAW

## Why your 808 disappears on phone speakers
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/808-disappears-on-phone-speakers.html
Phone speakers barely play below 200–300 Hz, so a clean 808 vanishes. Add a parallel harmonic layer, then check it through a phone filter.
Keywords: 808 not audible on phone, 808 phone speakers, 808 harmonics, parallel saturation 808, missing fundamental, small speaker translation, trap mixing, low end translation, CoProducer, ScrewAI, NoDAW

## How much headroom to leave for mastering (and why −6 dB isn’t the point)
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/how-much-headroom-to-leave-for-mastering.html
Headroom for mastering means no clipping and no mix-bus limiter. Peaks near −6 to −3 dBFS in 24-bit or float is convention; clipping can’t be undone.
Keywords: headroom for mastering, how much headroom mastering, -6 dB headroom, premaster, mix bus limiter, 32-bit float export, clipping, sending mix to mastering, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Integrated LUFS hides how loud the chorus actually is
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/integrated-lufs-hides-the-chorus.html
A master can read −14 LUFS integrated while its chorus runs 3–4 LU hotter. Measure integrated, short-term and momentary on one bounce first.
Keywords: integrated LUFS, short-term LUFS, momentary loudness, max short-term, BS.1770 gating, EBU R128, chorus loudness, ffmpeg ebur128, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Don’t match a streamed reference
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/dont-match-a-streamed-reference.html
A streamed reference was already turned down or up by the platform. Match it and you inherit an offset you never measured. Compare lossless files.
Keywords: reference track, streamed reference, loudness normalization, Spotify normalization, Sound Check, YouTube content loudness, loudness matching, reference mastering, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Short-term LUFS is not your target
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/short-term-lufs-is-not-your-target.html
Stores use integrated LUFS over the whole file. A hook at −9 short-term can still miss −14 integrated. Read both meters, then decide.
Keywords: short-term LUFS, integrated LUFS, momentary LUFS, streaming loudness, EBU R128, CoProducer, mastering

## Turn the mix down before you limit
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/turn-the-mix-down-before-you-limit.html
If the mix already hits 0 dBFS into the limiter, extra loudness is distortion you can’t take back. Pull the bus down 3–6 dB, then limit.
Keywords: gain staging, limiter headroom, mix bus level, true peak, clips, mastering, CoProducer, hip-hop, EDM

## What 432 Hz actually changes in a finished master
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/what-432-hz-actually-changes-in-a-master.html
Retuning a master from 440 to 432 Hz scales every frequency by 0.981818 (−31.77 cents) and, with resampling, adds 1.85% length. Measured on real renders.
Keywords: 432 Hz, 440 vs 432, what does 432 Hz do to music, retune master, cents, resampling, BPM, LUFS, reTUNE[432], NoDAW

## Resampling, pitch shifting, and tempo change are three different jobs
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/resampling-vs-pitch-shift-vs-tempo.html
Resampling moves pitch and time together, pitch shifting rebuilds time, tempo change keeps pitch. Seven FFmpeg renders measured for pitch, BPM, and smearing.
Keywords: resampling vs pitch shifting, time stretch, atempo, rubberband ffmpeg, asetrate, 432 Hz conversion, transient smearing, BPM drift, NoDAW

## Concert pitch before A=440: a history that never stood still
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/concert-pitch-history-before-a440.html
Before A=440, concert pitch ran from about 415 to 457 Hz. The dated record from Shore's 1711 fork to ISO 16, the temperature fights, and the 432 math.
Keywords: history of 440 Hz tuning, concert pitch history, A440, diapason normal 435, Stuttgart pitch, ISO 16, 432 Hz history, tuning fork 1711

## How to run a 432 vs 440 listening test you can trust
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/432-vs-440-blind-listening-test.html
432 Hz vs 440 Hz, tested fairly: level-match within 0.1 LU, switch at the same note, run a blind ABX round, and score it so placebo and loudness can't win.

## Which songs reveal a 432 Hz retune, and which hide it
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/songs-that-reveal-a-432-hz-retune.html
The best songs to test 432 Hz have exposed vocals, sustained chords and piano tails. Dense mixes and drums hide it. A measured way to build a test set.
Keywords: songs to test 432 Hz, songs in 432 Hz, 432 Hz test tracks, best music for 432 Hz, 432 Hz vocals, 432 Hz 808, 432 Hz comparison playlist

## 432 Hz mastering: LUFS and true peak after a retune
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/lufs-and-true-peak-after-432-retune.html
A 432 retune barely moves LUFS, but resampling can turn hidden inter-sample peaks into real overs. Render in float, measure, then normalize in two passes.

## Rumble you can’t hear is eating your limiter
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/subsonic-rumble-steals-limiter-headroom.html
Subsonic rumble and DC offset barely move LUFS but still count toward peaks. Check under 20–30 Hz and filter gently before the limiter to win headroom back.
Keywords: subsonic rumble, DC offset, high pass master, limiter headroom, true peak, low end, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Your bus compressor is pumping on the 808. High-pass the sidechain
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/bus-compressor-pumps-on-the-808.html
Hats and vocal air ducking on every 808 note means the low end is driving your bus compressor. A 60–150 Hz sidechain high-pass keeps the glue and stops the pump.
Keywords: bus compressor pumping, sidechain high pass filter, 808 mixing, mix bus compression, glue compressor, StemSplit, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Wide mixes fail in mono. Check mid/side before you bounce
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/wide-mixes-fail-in-mono.html
Stereo width that sounds huge on headphones can cancel on a phone. Measure mid/side balance, L/R correlation, and mono fold-down before you bounce.
Keywords: mono compatible mix, mid side balance, stereo width, phase correlation, phone speaker thin mix, StemSplit, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Clipper vs limiter for hip-hop delivery — loudness isn’t the only score
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/clipper-vs-limiter-hip-hop-delivery.html
Soft clipper vs brickwall limiter on the same drive: compare LUFS, true peak, and crest. Sample peak −1.0 dBFS is not true-peak safe.
Keywords: clipper vs limiter, hip-hop mastering, true peak, soft clip, alimiter, crest factor, ScrewAI, CoProducer, NoDAW

## Halftime still needs a legal peak
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/halftime-still-needs-a-legal-peak.html
A half-time slowdown changes length and weight, not the true-peak ceiling. Meter the screwed file before it goes anywhere public.

## When to slow the bounce
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/when-to-slow-the-bounce.html
Slow the print when the record wants weight, not when the mix is unfinished. A halftime desk is for the bounce, then the meter.

## The silence at the top of your bounce steals LUFS
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/leading-silence-steals-integrated-lufs.html
Digital silence is gated out of integrated LUFS, but quiet intros, long fades and ungated meters still pull the number down. Trim the edges, then measure.
Keywords: integrated LUFS, gating, leading silence, fade out, trim silence ffmpeg, NoDAW

## Your kick and 808 are arguing in the same chair
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/kick-and-808-same-chair.html
Kick and 808 fighting for 40–80 Hz? Decide who owns each hit with arrangement, carving or sidechain, then measure loudness so repair isn't hiding mud.
Keywords: kick and 808, low end masking, sidechain 808, trap mixing, StemSplit, NoDAW

## How loud should the vocal sit? Measure it against the beat
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/how-loud-should-the-vocal-sit.html
There’s no single right vocal level, but the vocal-to-beat loudness gap in LU is measurable. Match it to a reference, then fix only the buried bars.
Keywords: how loud should vocals be, vocal level in mix, vocal too quiet in chorus, LU, StemSplit, NoDAW

## Harsh S’s get louder after mastering. De-ess before the limiter
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/harsh-esses-get-louder-after-mastering.html
Vocals harsh after mastering? The master lifts level and top end, so borderline sibilance pops and eats true-peak headroom. Find the worst S’s and fix them in the mix.
Keywords: harsh vocals after mastering, sibilance, de-essing, de-ess before limiter, true peak, ScrewAI, NoDAW

## Why streaming platforms turn loud masters down
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/why-streaming-turns-loud-masters-down.html
Streaming services normalize toward −14 LUFS (Apple closer to −16). A hotter master is turned down, not played louder. Measure integrated LUFS before you limit again.
Keywords: LUFS, streaming loudness, Spotify normalization, mastering, CoProducer

## True peak is what codecs clip
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/true-peak-is-what-codecs-clip.html
True peak (dBTP) estimates inter-sample peaks. Streaming wants about −1.0 dBTP. A legal sample peak can still clip after AAC or Opus reconstruction.
Keywords: true peak, dBTP, inter-sample peaks, AAC, codecs

## What a 70-to-90 CoProducer repair actually changes
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/what-a-70-to-90-repair-changes.html
Public A/B proofs: Crazy Stacy 70→90 (831 clips→0), BeatGoHard 77→95, Drippin 66→93. A delivery pass — not a remix or taste rewrite.
Keywords: CoProducer repair, release score, clipping, loudnorm, A/B

## Should you upload an unreleased master to the cloud?
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/should-you-upload-an-unreleased-master.html
Upload an unreleased master only if you accept a vendor holding the file. Loudness, true peak, and clip checks can stay fully local with CoProducer.
Keywords: local mastering, privacy, unreleased master, cloud upload, CoProducer

## A release checklist that matches the meter
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/release-checklist-that-matches-the-meter.html
Release checklist: −14 LUFS ±1.5, true peak ≤ −1.0 dBTP, 0 clipped samples, ≥44.1 kHz, phase ≥ 0.2, score ≥ 90. Same gates CoProducer scores.
Keywords: release checklist, LUFS, true peak, phase correlation, delivery

## Crest factor is not loudness
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/crest-factor-is-not-loudness.html
Crest factor is peak-to-RMS height. LUFS is perceived loudness over time. You can raise crest and still miss −14 LUFS — or hit −14 with a crushed crest.
Keywords: crest factor, dynamic range, LUFS, loudness, punch

## Phase correlation is a mono audition
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/phase-correlation-and-mono.html
Phase near 0 or negative means the mix thins or cancels in mono. CoProducer fails values under about 0.2. Auto-repair will not flip polarity for you.
Keywords: phase correlation, mono compatibility, stereo width, mixing

## Quiet masters get turned up — and so does the noise
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/quiet-masters-and-noise-floor.html
Streaming turn-up lifts quiet files. A −20 LUFS master may be gained up, which also lifts hiss, rumble, and room tone. Quiet is not a free pass.
Keywords: noise floor, quiet masters, loudness normalization, hiss

## When not to reach for the limiter
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/when-not-to-reach-for-the-limiter.html
Skip another limiter when clips are already non-zero, LUFS is only slightly hot, or the real problem is arrangement, noise, or a bad edit — not peak height.
Keywords: limiter, mastering, clipping, dynamics, repair

## Sample rate and bit depth are delivery hygiene
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/sample-rate-and-bit-depth-for-delivery.html
CoProducer fails sample rates under 44.1 kHz. Why 32 kHz fails delivery, when 44.1/48/96 are fine, what bit depth distributors want, and how to verify the bounce.
Keywords: sample rate, bit depth, 44.1 kHz, delivery, masters

## Reference matching without guesswork
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/reference-matching-without-guesswork.html
Reference matching means comparing meters, not vibes. CoProducer’s divergence table shows where your bounce sits versus a reference on real gates.
Keywords: reference matching, mix reference, LUFS compare, spectral balance

## Album consistency is a batch problem
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/album-consistency-in-one-meter.html
Album consistency means every track clears the same delivery gates and sits in a similar loudness lane — a batch measurement problem, not one “final” bounce.
Keywords: album mastering, batch analysis, loudness consistency, CoProducer

## Why HTML, JSON, and TXT all matter
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/why-three-report-formats.html
HTML is for humans and clients. JSON is for pipelines. TXT is for quick notes and tickets. CoProducer writes all three so the same facts travel cleanly.

Local .bat and desktop tools skip upload queues, retention policies, and per-track metering fees. Keep measurement, stems, and syrup renders on your machine.

## Stems diagnose mixes — they do not replace them
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/stems-diagnose-mixes-do-not-replace-them.html
Stem separation isolates parts so you can hear collisions. It does not invent a better arrangement. Use stems to diagnose, then fix the mix.
Keywords: stem separation, StemSplit, mix diagnosis, NoDAW

## Screw tempo still needs a legal peak
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/screw-tempo-still-needs-a-legal-peak.html
Slowing a track for syrup aesthetics changes duration and crest, not true-peak law. A screwed render still needs ≤ −1.0 dBTP before upload.

## Vertical video is a loudness trap
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/vertical-video-is-a-loudness-trap.html
Shorts, Reels, and Stories normalize differently from music stores, but crushed dialog and clipped music still fail. Measure before you post vertical.

## Mastering .bat versus opening the session
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/mastering-bat-vs-opening-the-session.html
A mastering .bat is for trusted delivery passes on finished mixes. Open the session when arrangement, bad edits, or clipped vocals need real surgery.

## How to read a CoProducer score
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/how-to-read-a-coproducer-score.html
A CoProducer score ≥ 90 means release-ready against the tool’s gates — not a Grammy. Read the findings: a 70 with 831 clips is a different emergency than a 77.
Keywords: CoProducer score, release ready, audio analysis, gates

## Re-encoding eats true-peak headroom
URL: https://myaiplug.github.io/coproducer-web/blog/reencoding-eats-true-peak-headroom.html
Every lossy encode can invent new inter-sample peaks. Leaving only 0.1 dB of true-peak margin is how a ‘clean’ WAV becomes a clipped stream.
Keywords: re-encoding, true peak, AAC, headroom, delivery
